Example: Got the job today, big W!
Context: Typically used in conversations to celebrate success, achievements, or positive outcomes
Informal_Text: Nailed it today, big win!
Informal_Text_Without_Slang: Landed the job today, big success!
Formal_Text: Secured the employment position today, significant success!

Example: I forgot my wallet at home, that’s an L.
Context: Often used when referring to a failure or mishap, either personally or generally
Informal_Text: Dang it, left my wallet at home – that's a loss for sure!
Informal_Text_Without_Slang: Oops, I left my wallet at home, that's a bummer.
Formal_Text: I left my wallet at home; that's a setback.

Description: Response to a comment or action on the internet that is particularly bad.
Example: Your tweet got 5 likes and 100 replies calling you out. L + ratio.
Context: Popularized on social media platforms to signify that someone not only failed but also had their failure amplified through backlash.
Informal_Text: Dang, your tweet only managed five likes but a hundred people called you out on it. Big ol' ratio, mate!
Informal_Text_Without_Slang: Your tweet garnered 5 likes but attracted a hundred responses pointing out your mistake, big time.
Formal_Text: Your tweet earned five likes but was met with one hundred replies critiquing your statement, indicating a substantial discrepancy in the quality of your content.

Description: excellent or of very high quality
Example: That meme is so dank!
Context: Commonly used in internet slang to refer to memes or humor that are edgy or particularly funny.
Informal_Text: That meme's fire as hell!
Informal_Text_Without_Slang: That meme's utterly fantastic!
Formal_Text: That meme is remarkably impressive!

Description: Derogatory term for Millennials. Used when millennials are perceived to be excessively attempting to be trendy or stylish.
Example: That phrase is so cheugy, no one says that anymore.
Context: Used to refer to things that were once popular but are now considered passé, usually in a millennial vs. Gen Z context.
Informal_Text: Man, that's totally cringey – nobody's using that these days.
Informal_Text_Without_Slang: That's so uncool and outdated, nobody uses that expression anymore.
Formal_Text: That expression seems unfashionable and outdated, as it's no longer commonly used.

Example: TFW you finish a big project and can finally relax
Context: Often paired with an image or caption to convey an emotion or experience, mostly used in memes.
Informal_Text: Man, when you wrap up a major project and finally get to unwind...
Informal_Text_Without_Slang: When you complete a large task, there's that satisfying feeling of relief when you can finally unwind.
Formal_Text: Upon completion of an extensive undertaking, there arises a sense of relief and tranquility.

Example: He’s really woke about climate change.
Context: Originally used in activist circles, it has since been co-opted and sometimes used sarcastically.
Informal_Text: He's truly in-the-know when it comes to climate change.
Informal_Text_Without_Slang: He's truly informed and concerned about climate change.
Formal_Text: He is remarkably informed and conscious about climate change issues.

Example: This new track is a total bop!
Context: Commonly used in reference to music, especially upbeat songs that are hard to resist dancing to.
Informal_Text: Man, this new track is pure fire!
Informal_Text_Without_Slang: This fresh track is a real earworm!
Formal_Text: This new track is an absolute gem!

Example: Michael Jordan is the GOAT of basketball.
Context: Frequently used in sports but has expanded to any field where someone is considered the best.
Informal_Text: Mike Jordan's the baddest in hoops, no doubt!
Informal_Text_Without_Slang: Michael Jordan is the greatest basketball player of all time.
Formal_Text: Michael Jordan is undoubtedly the greatest basketball player of all time.

Description: Something that is small, and in most cases exceptionally adorable.
Example: Look at that smol puppy, it’s adorable!
Context: Typically used when describing pets, babies, or anything tiny and endearing.
Informal_Text: Check out that tiny, cute pup!
Informal_Text_Without_Slang: Check out that tiny, utterly charming pup!
Formal_Text: Behold the diminutive puppy; it is remarkably charming.

Description: Fam is a shorter word for family, but don't be fooled– it can be used to describe your friends or the way Millennials use "bro".
Example: What’s good, fam? Long time no see!
Context: Used in casual conversation to address close friends or acquaintances.
Informal_Text: Hey there, what's up my folks? Been a minute!
Informal_Text_Without_Slang: How's it going, folks? Been a while!
Formal_Text: Greetings, dear friends! It's been a while.

Description: a makeover or transformation from bad to good.
Example: She really had a glow up since high school.
Context: Mostly used when someone has improved their looks, style, or general confidence.
Informal_Text: Man, she's sure transformed since high school!
Informal_Text_Without_Slang: She's certainly transformed quite a bit since high school.
Formal_Text: She has significantly transformed for the better since her high school days.

Description: Supporting something. Specifically used in some cases to the idolatry support of personalities.
Example: I stan BTS so hard!
Context: Originally from an Eminem song, it refers to obsessive fans but has since been reclaimed to mean intense admiration.
Informal_Text: I'm totally obsessed with BTS!
Informal_Text_Without_Slang: I'm a die-hard fan of BTS!
Formal_Text: I am an ardent admirer of BTS.

Description: common amongst the earlier talking stages of a relationship. Ghosting someone means you start ignoring them or stop texting them back.
Example: We were talking for weeks, and then she just ghosted me.
Context: Used in online dating or friendships where one party disappears with no warning.
Informal_Text: We chatted up a storm for weeks, and then poof! She vanished off the face of the conversation.
Informal_Text_Without_Slang: We chatted for weeks, and then suddenly she disappeared without a trace.
Formal_Text: After several weeks of communication, I found myself abruptly cut off without explanation.

Example: He’s just salty because he lost the game
Context: Often used in competitive environments or when someone is overly upset about a minor issue.
Informal_Text: He's real green over losing the game
Informal_Text_Without_Slang: He's feeling a bit sour due to losing the game
Formal_Text: He seems rather envious due to his loss in the game.

Example: I’m just here to sip tea and watch the drama unfold.
Context: Can be used in gossip situations or when someone is staying out of a conflict but observing it.
Informal_Text: Just here for the lowdown and enjoying the show!
Informal_Text_Without_Slang: I'm just here to chat and see what's going on.
Formal_Text: I'm merely here for a discussion and observe the events as they transpire.

Description: Another way of saying swag, drip is a term for a cool or sexy trend or style.
Example: His drip today is on point.
Context: Used in fashion circles to compliment someone’s style or outfit.
Informal_Text: His style's killer today.
Informal_Text_Without_Slang: His style today is really cool.
Formal_Text: His style today is particularly stylish.

Description: Acronym for "If you know, you know." Used to describe inside jokes.
Example: That hidden message in the movie was iconic. IYKYK.
Context: Generally used to reference inside jokes or niche knowledge.
Informal_Text: That secret movie scene was legendarily dope. Only those in the know get it.
Informal_Text_Without_Slang: That secret message in the movie was legendary - you had to be there to get it.
Formal_Text: The cryptic message within that film was quite remarkable - one that only those privy to its meaning would truly appreciate.

Description: To be constantly thinking or upset about something.
Example: That song is living rent-free in my head
Context: Commonly used for anything that someone keeps thinking about obsessively.
Informal_Text: Man, that tune's driving me nuts, won't stop playing in here!
Informal_Text_Without_Slang: That tune's been playing on repeat in my mind
Formal_Text: That song persistently occupies my thoughts

Description: Used to threaten physical combat with someone
Example: If you keep talking like that, you’re gonna catch these hands.
Context: Used in confrontational or playful situations when someone is threatening physical action.
Informal_Text: You better watch how you're talkin', or you'll find out I ain't playin'.
Informal_Text_Without_Slang: You're pushing your luck there, mate. I might just have to teach you a lesson.
Formal_Text: Should your conduct persist in this manner, I shall be compelled to engage in physical confrontation with you.

Description: If you drag someone, you're criticizing or making fun of them
Example: She dragged him for his terrible performance.
Context: Often used in social media when someone is publicly called out or ridiculed.
Informal_Text: She ripped into him over his lousy show.
Informal_Text_Without_Slang: She really tore into him for that poor showing.
Formal_Text: She critically scrutinized him for his substandard presentation.

Description: Used to say something is good. Primarily used to describe food
Example: This pizza is bussin’!
Context: Primarily used to compliment delicious food, but can apply to anything impressive.
Informal_Text: Man, this pizza's fire!
Informal_Text_Without_Slang: This pizza is fabulous!
Formal_Text: This pizza is exceptional!

Description: If someone is looking snatched, they look really good, particularly their outfit
Example: Her makeup was snatched at the event.
Context: Often used in beauty and fashion to indicate someone looks flawless.
Informal_Text: She was serving looks with her makeup at the event.
Informal_Text_Without_Slang: Her makeup slayed at the event.
Formal_Text: Her makeup was notably striking at the event.

Description: a form of shaming the actions or opinions of a public figure, company, or organization
Example: People are saying he’s canceled after those comments.
Context: A highly debated topic where individuals are held accountable, often through social media boycotts.
Informal_Text: Peeps are giving him the boot over that remark.
Informal_Text_Without_Slang: Folks are calling him out for those remarks, effectively ending his career or public support.
Formal_Text: Individuals are advocating for the public disapproval of him following his remarks.

Example: FFS, why is this meeting taking so long?
Context: Used informally, especially in text or online communication to show irritation.
Informal_Text: Bloody hell, why's this meeting dragging on?
Informal_Text_Without_Slang: Good grief, why is this meeting dragging on?
Formal_Text: Good heavens, why is this meeting prolonged to such an extent?

Description: similar to emo or goth culture, but they use the internet to express themselves.
Example: He’s such an e-boy with those black nails and chains.
Context: Describes a fashion or online subculture associated with platforms like TikTok and Instagram.
Informal_Text: Dude's totally rocking that e-boy vibe with those dark nail polish and chains!
Informal_Text_Without_Slang: He's clearly embracing the online gothic aesthetic with those black nails and chains.
Formal_Text: He appears to be following a style reminiscent of emo or goth culture, as indicated by his black nail polish and chain accessories.

Description: similar to emo or goth culture, but they use the internet to express themselves.
Example: She’s such an e-girl with her neon eyeliner and platform boots.
Context: Commonly associated with social media platforms like TikTok, where users embrace a specific style influenced by internet and alternative culture.
Informal_Text: She's totally an internet vibe gal with those bright eye liner flick and skyscraper shoes!
Informal_Text_Without_Slang: She's very much into the digital emo or goth subculture, with her brightly colored eyeliners and elevated boots.
Formal_Text: She exhibits characteristics reminiscent of individuals associated with digital or online emo or goth culture, as evidenced by her use of neon eyeliner and platform boots.

Example: She wore the same dress as the bride at the wedding? Big yikes.
Context: Used in situations where something is particularly awkward or cringeworthy.
Informal_Text: Whoa, she rocked up in the same dress as the bride at the wedding? Major awkward moment!
Informal_Text_Without_Slang: That's quite awkward – she wore the same dress as the bride at the wedding.
Formal_Text: That's rather unfortunate - she wore the same dress as the bride at the wedding.

Description: shortened term for saying "I'm going to"
Example: I’m finna head out.
Context: Often used in informal speech to indicate imminent action, popular in certain dialects of English.
Informal_Text: Gonna bolt soon.
Informal_Text_Without_Slang: About to leave.
Formal_Text: I am about to leave.

Example: He said he’s a millionaire, but that’s cap.
Context: Frequently used in conversations to call out someone who is lying or exaggerating.
Informal_Text: He claims to be a milly, but that's bullsh*t.
Informal_Text_Without_Slang: He claims to be a millionaire, but that's pure nonsense.
Formal_Text: He claims to be a millionaire, but it's an exaggeration.

Example: I high-key love this song.
Context: Used to express that something is not being hidden or downplayed.
Informal_Text: Man, I seriously dig this tune!
Informal_Text_Without_Slang: I really, genuinely love this song.
Formal_Text: I genuinely enjoy this song.

Description: Sycophancy, being overly affectionate in pursuit of a sexual relationship
Example: He buys her gifts every day, he’s such a simp.
Context: Typically used as a derogatory term for someone who tries too hard to impress or please someone they’re attracted to.
Informal_Text: He's constantly showering her with gifts, what a hopeless romantic!
Informal_Text_Without_Slang: He's quite the fawning admirer, isn't he, constantly showering her with presents.
Formal_Text: He consistently showers her with gifts daily, displaying a marked lack of self-respect in his pursuit of affection.

Description: Something that is ironically trendy. One might consider Crocs to be of the camp aesthetic.
Example: That outfit is so camp, it’s amazing.
Context: Often used in fashion, particularly in avant-garde or over-the-top styles that are playful or flamboyant.
Informal_Text: This get-up is totally kitschy, I love it!
Informal_Text_Without_Slang: That ensemble is incredibly kitschy, it's quite remarkable.
Formal_Text: That ensemble exhibits an ironic trendiness that is truly remarkable.

Description: a person that you find attractive
Example: He showed up to the party looking like a whole snack.
Context: A compliment used in dating or flirting contexts, implying someone is good-looking and appealing.
Informal_Text: He turned heads at the party, looking like a total charmer.
Informal_Text_Without_Slang: He turned up at the party being quite the looker.
Formal_Text: He appeared at the gathering as quite an appealing individual.

Description: If someone is really getting on your nerves, you might tell them to take several seats.
Example: You’re being way too extra right now, take several seats.
Context: Often used in arguments or when someone is being overly dramatic or intrusive.
Informal_Text: You're being a real drama queen today, please find another chair.
Informal_Text_Without_Slang: You're making quite a scene at the moment, kindly find another spot to sit.
Formal_Text: Your behavior is becoming excessively dramatic at present; kindly find a more discreet location to reside for some time.

Description: To praise someone when they are doing something good. The one being praised is to do the "ice in my veins" pose popularized by Basketball player D'Angelo Russell.
Example: Sheesh, that’s a lot of money!
Context: Can be used in response to something impressive or unexpected, especially when exaggerated for effect.
Informal_Text: Wowza, that's some serious cash!
Informal_Text_Without_Slang: Wow, that's some serious cash!
Formal_Text: Indeed, that's quite an impressive sum!

Description: Something that is better in a peculiar manner
Example: This song hits different at night.
Context: Often used when comparing emotional experiences or moods tied to specific circumstances.
Informal_Text: This tune sure packs a punch at nighttime.
Informal_Text_Without_Slang: This song feels unique in a special way during the night.
Formal_Text: This song has a unique impact in the evening.

Example: You want to meet at 6? Bet.
Context: Used to confirm plans or agreements in a laid-back way.
Informal_Text: Sure thing, I'm down for 6.
Informal_Text_Without_Slang: Alrighty then, let's meet up at six.
Formal_Text: I'd be happy to meet at 6. Agreed.

Description: Used to add emphasis to something
Example: That’s the best movie of all time, periodt.
Context: Often used to add emphasis to a statement, signaling that there’s no further debate.
Informal_Text: That's hands down the top movie ever, point blank!
Informal_Text_Without_Slang: Absolutely, that's hands down the greatest film ever, full stop.
Formal_Text: Absolutely undoubtedly, that's the finest film ever made.

Description: Finesse means to trick or manipulate someone or a situation in order to get what you want.
Example: He finessed his way into the VIP section.
Context: Typically used when someone gets what they want through charm, skill, or slyness.
Informal_Text: He pulled off a smooth move to get into the VIP area.
Informal_Text_Without_Slang: He managed to sneakily make his way into the VIP area.
Formal_Text: He skillfully maneuvered himself into the exclusive area.

Description: Similar to "I'm dead", this is just another term to use when you find something hilarious
Example: That joke had me weak!
Context: Commonly used when something makes you laugh hard, often exaggerated in digital conversations.
Informal_Text: Man, that joke killed me!
Informal_Text_Without_Slang: That joke had me cracking up!
Formal_Text: The joke left me utterly amused!

Description: a phrase used to describe someone who is generally well-liked and charismatic. It can also be used to describe someone when they're making a scene, but not necessarily in a bad way
Example: She’s living her life like she’s the main character in a movie.
Context: Often used in social media to refer to people who seem to be leading an extraordinary or dramatic life.
Informal_Text: She's playing her own show for sure!
Informal_Text_Without_Slang: She's playing her part as if she's the leading lady in a film.
Formal_Text: She appears to be leading her life as if she were the protagonist in a film.

Description: A shortened version of "sister", this term is typically used to greet a friend, no matter their gender.
Example: Sis, you are killing it in that outfit!
Context: Commonly used among women as a term of camaraderie or affection.
Informal_Text: Hey girl, you're rockin' that look!
Informal_Text_Without_Slang: Hey there, you're rocking that look amazingly!
Formal_Text: Dear friend, you look wonderful in that attire!

Description: Another term to use if you find something particularly funny.
Example: That meme is sending me!
Context: Used in response to something humorous or amusing, often in digital contexts.
Informal_Text: That meme's cracking me up!
Informal_Text_Without_Slang: That meme is cracking me up!
Formal_Text: That meme is remarkably amusing!

Example: I’m trying to stack up this gaup before the weekend.
Context: Used in casual conversation, particularly among younger people, to refer to money or making money.
Informal_Text: I'm hustling for some serious cheddar by Friday.
Informal_Text_Without_Slang: I'm aiming to accumulate some serious cash before the weekend.
Formal_Text: I'm attempting to accumulate a substantial amount of funds before the weekend.

Description: Another way of giving disapproval for something.
Example: That outfit? This ain’t it, chief.
Context: Often used in social media or casual conversation to reject an idea, style, or trend.
Informal_Text: That getup, nah, this ain't poppin', mate.
Informal_Text_Without_Slang: That getup isn't quite right, boss.
Formal_Text: That ensemble is not quite fitting, sir.

Description: Someone who is out there and enjoys taking things to a new level of flamboyance.
Example: She brought a whole suitcase for a weekend trip, she’s so extra.
Context: Used to describe behavior that is excessive or unnecessary.
Informal_Text: She packed like a drama queen for a weekend away, she's really over-the-top!
Informal_Text_Without_Slang: She brought an entire luggage for a weekend getaway; she's quite over-the-top.
Formal_Text: She packed excessively for a weekend trip, displaying an exuberant and flamboyant nature.

Description: Swift and witty response to an insult or critique
Example: Her clapback to that troll was savage.
Context: Often used in social media to describe a sharp retort, usually in the context of online arguments.
Informal_Text: She fired back at that jerk with a zinger.
Informal_Text_Without_Slang: Her sharp retort to that troll was biting.
Formal_Text: Her retort to that critic was sharp and witty.

Description: Pronounced "at me." Used on social media when someone feels attacked by a post.
Example: I’m about to pull up, C me at the club!
Context: Informal and often used in texting or casual conversations to refer to meeting someone.
Informal_Text: Hit me up when you get there, let's link at the club!
Informal_Text_Without_Slang: I'll be showing up, find me at the club!
Formal_Text: Kindly meet me at the club when you arrive.

Description: Has two definitions. It can be used as a shortened version of "as hell." It can also be used as an acronym for age/sex/location.
Example: It’s cold asl outside!
Context: Used to intensify a statement, typically in casual conversation or texts.
Informal_Text: Damn, it's freezing out there!
Informal_Text_Without_Slang: Man, it's freezing out there!
Formal_Text: Indeed, it's exceptionally chilly outside!

Description: To get in a physical altercation with someone.
Example: He was out there bangin’ 30s all night.
Context: Typically used in contexts involving gangs or street culture, referring to gun violence.
Informal_Text: He went at it hammer and tongs all night long.
Informal_Text_Without_Slang: He sure had a fight-filled night.
Formal_Text: He engaged in numerous physical confrontations throughout the night.

Description: Originally meaning "to be your self and not care about how others view you", The word is now used to indicate an opinion or something that someone agrees with. It is especially common in political slang and discussions.
Example: He doesn’t care what anyone thinks, he’s so based.
Context: Popularized online, often in political or philosophical discussions, to praise someone for being genuine or sticking to their principles.
Informal_Text: He don't give a damn 'bout what folks think, he's straight up real.
Informal_Text_Without_Slang: He truly doesn't give a hoot about other people's opinions; he's just being genuine.
Formal_Text: He demonstrates an admirable disregard for public opinion, being particularly independent.

Description: To apply makeup to the face.
Example: I’m about to beat my face for this event tonight.
Context: Commonly used in beauty and makeup communities to refer to a skillfully applied makeup look.
Informal_Text: I'm gonna slay my makeup for tonight's event.
Informal_Text_Without_Slang: I'm fixing to put on some makeup for tonight's event.
Formal_Text: I am planning to apply makeup meticulously for this evening's event.

Description: Term used to describe when someone is excessively angry.
Example: He’s big mad because we beat his team last night.
Context: Used to emphasize how upset someone is, often in a playful or teasing manner.
Informal_Text: He's seriously pissed off that we beat his squad last night.
Informal_Text_Without_Slang: He's really furious that our team defeated his last night.
Formal_Text: He is profoundly angry because our team defeated his last night.

Description: A euphemism for how many people one has had sex with. Initially referred to specifically sexual intercourse, but was expanded to include all forms of sex.
Example: What’s your body count?
Context: Often used in conversations about sexual experiences or romantic history.
Informal_Text: How many notches do you have on your belt?
Informal_Text_Without_Slang: How many people have you been intimate with?
Formal_Text: How many intimate encounters have you experienced?

Example: We’re going to a boujee restaurant tonight.
Context: Often used to describe someone or something as luxurious or exclusive.
Informal_Text: Heading out to that swanky joint tonight, eh?
Informal_Text_Without_Slang: We're dining at an upscale eatery tonight.
Formal_Text: We are dining at an elegant establishment tonight.

Example: He was joking about his bussy all night.
Context: Usually used humorously or in LGBT+ communities as part of casual or sexual discussions.
Informal_Text: He cracked jokes about his backside all evening.
Informal_Text_Without_Slang: He cracked jokes about his rear all night.
Formal_Text: He made humorous references to his anus throughout the evening.

Description: A response to embarrassment or social awkwardness
Example: That performance was so cringe.
Context: Often used to describe content, behavior, or situations that cause second-hand embarrassment.
Informal_Text: Man, that performance was super awkward!
Informal_Text_Without_Slang: That performance was incredibly awkward.
Formal_Text: That performance elicited a strong sense of discomfort due to its awkwardness.

Description: Used to describe something humorous to such an extent as to "kill you."
Example: That joke had me ded.
Context: Used online to express that something is so funny it “killed” you from laughter.
Informal_Text: That gag nearly knocked me out cold!
Informal_Text_Without_Slang: That joke was absolutely hilarious.
Formal_Text: That joke was extremely funny.

Example: Pizza is the best food ever. Facts.
Context: Used to emphasize agreement or that something is undeniably true.
Informal_Text: Damn straight, pizza's the bomb! Truth!
Informal_Text_Without_Slang: Pizza truly is the greatest food out there, don't argue with me on that!
Formal_Text: Pizza is undoubtedly the finest culinary delight available. This is an indisputable truth.

Description: A major improvement in one's self, usually an improvement in appearance, confidence, and style. Frequently used in a context relating to puberty.
Example: She had a major glow-up over the summer.
Context: Mostly used to talk about someone’s improvement in looks or self-esteem.
Informal_Text: Man, she really transformed this summer!
Informal_Text_Without_Slang: She underwent a significant transformation in appearance during the summer.
Formal_Text: She underwent a significant transformation in her appearance during the summer.

Description: Used to express shock, embarrassment, and or amusement.
Example: She spilled her drink on her dress and I oop!
Context: Popularized by meme culture, often used humorously when something unexpected happens.
Informal_Text: Whoa, she just spilled her drink on her dress, and I'm like whoopsie!
Informal_Text_Without_Slang: Whoa, she spilled her drink on her dress, oh my!
Formal_Text: She spilled her drink onto her dress, and I was taken aback!

Description: Describes the vibes or connotation of something.
Example: It’s giving 90s nostalgia with that outfit.
Context: Often used in fashion or style discussions to refer to the overall impression or vibe something conveys.
Informal_Text: That fit's totally vibing some '90s throwback!
Informal_Text_Without_Slang: That outfit has a definite '90s throwback feel to it.
Formal_Text: The ensemble evokes a strong sense of 1990s nostalgia.

Description: Colloquially: "Enlightened", "Hot", "Fire." The new hotness; something remarkable, interesting, fun or amusing. Generally positive.
Example: That party was lit!
Context: Common in younger generations to describe a positive experience or event.
Informal_Text: Man, that party was on fire!
Informal_Text_Without_Slang: That party was fantastic!
Formal_Text: That party was quite remarkable!

Example: That movie was mid, nothing special.
Context: Often used when discussing entertainment, like music, movies, or games.
Informal_Text: That flick ain't all that, pretty ordinary.
Informal_Text_Without_Slang: That film wasn't anything extraordinary, quite ordinary.
Formal_Text: The film was average, lacking anything extraordinary.

Description: Used to condemn or poke fun at someone or something.
Example: Not you eating the last slice of pizza!
Context: Used in a teasing or humorous way in informal conversation.
Informal_Text: Ain't that some other guy gobbling up the last piece of pizza!
Informal_Text_Without_Slang: You didn't have to go and eat the last slice of pizza, did you?
Formal_Text: That is hardly seemly of you to consume the final piece of pizza!

Description: Someone who cannot think for themselves and/or has no or little control over their own life. Someone that is ready to agree with popular opinion unquestioningly and always believes what they are told. Gullible
Example: She’s acting like such an NPC, just going with the flow.
Context: Used to describe people who seem to follow a script or act predictably without any autonomy.
Informal_Text: She's really just a sheep following the herd.
Informal_Text_Without_Slang: She's behaving so mindlessly obedient, following the crowd blindly.
Formal_Text: She is exhibiting a disturbing level of conformity, blindly following trends without questioning them.

Description: Derogatory term directed towards Baby Boomers. Used as a response when boomers are deemed to be out of touch with younger generations
Example: You don’t understand memes? OK boomer.
Context: Used by younger generations to respond to outdated opinions or criticism from older people.
Informal_Text: You clueless on internet humor, huh? Alright, Gen Xer or Millennial here.
Informal_Text_Without_Slang: You're clueless about memes? Alright, generation X or Y then.
Formal_Text: Understanding memes appears to be beyond you; very well, Generation Baby Boomers.

Description: Short for "I swear to god." Means that a person's statement is frank.
Example: I’m telling you, that was the best movie I’ve ever seen, on god!
Context: Used to emphasize that what someone is saying is absolutely true or serious. Often said in moments of intensity or when trying to convince others of your sincerity.
Informal_Text: That was straight up the best movie I've ever seen, cross my heart!
Informal_Text_Without_Slang: I'm seriously telling you, that was the best movie I've ever seen - I swear to goodness!
Formal_Text: Indeed, that film was undoubtedly the most exceptional one I have ever witnessed.

Description: When an internet post has a comparable number of comments/replies to "likes", which is usually indicative of a poor reception.
Example: That tweet got ratio’d so bad, more people replied than liked it.
Context: Common on Twitter, indicating that a post was unpopular or disagreed with.
Informal_Text: Man, that tweet was roasted something fierce; way more comments than likes!
Informal_Text_Without_Slang: That tweet received a lot of criticism, with more comments than likes.
Formal_Text: The tweet attracted significantly more comments than likes, indicating a less favorable response.

Example: He’s got so much rizz, everyone likes him.
Context: Mostly used in discussions about dating and flirting.
Informal_Text: Dude's got charisma by the bucketload, everybody digs him.
Informal_Text_Without_Slang: His charm is irresistible; it wins over everyone.
Formal_Text: His charm is undeniable, and it endears him to all.

Example: I spilled my drink sksksk.
Context: Often associated with VSCO girl culture, it’s used in casual, playful conversation.
Informal_Text: Oh man, I just spilled my drink, hahaha!
Informal_Text_Without_Slang: Oh, I've accidentally spilled my drink! Ha ha!
Formal_Text: I giggled upon spilling my drink.

Description: Used to refer to something (typically music) that is perceived to be good.
Example: This new track slaps!
Context: Mostly used when talking about music or experiences that are enjoyable and energetic.
Informal_Text: This new track kills it!
Informal_Text_Without_Slang: This new track rocks!
Formal_Text: This new track is excellent!

Example: Why’s he acting so sus all of a sudden?
Context: Became widely popular due to the game Among Us, often used to describe behavior that seems off.
Informal_Text: What's up with him suddenly acting fishy?
Informal_Text_Without_Slang: Why's he suddenly looking shifty and suspicious?
Formal_Text: Why has he suddenly begun acting suspiciously?

Example: She’s slaying in that outfit tonight!
Context: Often used to praise someone’s appearance, performance, or confidence.
Informal_Text: She's killing it in that outfit tonight!
Informal_Text_Without_Slang: She's absolutely nailing it with that outfit tonight!
Formal_Text: She is truly impressive in that attire tonight.

Example: Spill the tea, I need to know what happened!
Context: Common in social media and casual conversation when discussing secrets or gossip.
Informal_Text: Dish the dirt, what's the lowdown? I gotta know!
Informal_Text_Without_Slang: Dish the dirt, please fill me in on what went down!
Formal_Text: Please share the details, I am eager to learn about the recent events!

Description: To understand what was supposed to be done; to do something well
Example: That outfit is fire, she really understood the assignment.
Context: Often used to praise someone for excelling at a task, particularly when it comes to fashion or performance.
Informal_Text: That fit's poppin', she nailed it for sure.
Informal_Text_Without_Slang: She aced that outfit's style brief for sure.
Formal_Text: She truly grasped the intended style with that outfit.

Example: Those sneakers are valid!
Context: Typically used as an endorsement or to confirm something is acceptable or impressive.
Informal_Text: Those kicks are cool!
Informal_Text_Without_Slang: Those sneakers make sense!
Formal_Text: Those sneakers are indeed sensible and understandable!

Description: To check one's personality or attitude
Example: Vibe check: Are you good?
Context: Often used in casual settings to gauge how someone is feeling or what the general atmosphere is.
Informal_Text: What's your mood today? Feeling alright?
Informal_Text_Without_Slang: How's your mood today?
Formal_Text: Inquiring about your current disposition: How are you feeling today?

Description: describes a generic positive feeling that someone has about something
Example: We were just vibing to some music all night.
Context: Used to describe a relaxed, enjoyable state of mind or atmosphere.
Informal_Text: We were totally grooving to some tunes all night long.
Informal_Text_Without_Slang: We had a great time grooving to some tunes all evening.
Formal_Text: We spent the entire night enjoying the music together.

Description: To do something so well as to "make one's wig fly off."
Example: That performance was amazing, wig!
Context: Popular in stan culture, especially on social media, to react to something shocking or exciting.
Informal_Text: Man, that performance was off the charts, it'd blow someone's hat right off!
Informal_Text_Without_Slang: Man, that performance was off the charts incredible!
Formal_Text: That performance was truly extraordinary, indeed!

Example: Let’s meet at 7. Word
Context: A laid-back affirmation used in casual conversations.
Informal_Text: Alrighty then, see you at 7. Word!
Informal_Text_Without_Slang: Sounds good, let's hook up at 7 then. Cheers!
Formal_Text: Shall we meet at seven? Understood.

Example: I’m tired af after that workout.
Context: Commonly used in digital communication to stress intensity.
Informal_Text: I'm absolutely knackered from that workout.
Informal_Text_Without_Slang: I'm knackered to bits after that workout.
Formal_Text: I'm absolutely exhausted following that workout.

Description: When you have done something silly making you feel like your own brain shrinks as you regret all of your life
Example: He solved that puzzle in seconds, big brain moves.
Context: Often used humorously to praise someone’s intelligence or creativity.
Informal_Text: Dang, he cracked that riddle in a blink, genius-level stuff!
Informal_Text_Without_Slang: Dang, he figured out that puzzle in mere seconds, quite clever of him!
Formal_Text: Displayed an extraordinary level of intellectual acumen in solving that puzzle so swiftly.

Description: Used to describe your typical alpha male
Example: He’s such a Chad, always winning at everything.
Context: Mostly used online to refer to hyper-masculine or alpha male behavior, sometimes sarcastically.
Informal_Text: Dude's just too much of a stud, always coming out on top in everything.
Informal_Text_Without_Slang: He's always triumphant, never losing at anything.
Formal_Text: He is indeed an exemplary and successful gentleman, consistently excelling in various endeavors.

Description: To be completely and utterly destroyed.
Example: That car is clapped, it’s falling apart.
Context: Used casually to describe something as worn-out or unattractive.
Informal_Text: Man, that car's a total wreck!
Informal_Text_Without_Slang: That car's a complete write-off, it's on its last legs.
Formal_Text: That automobile has deteriorated significantly; it appears to be in a state of disrepair.

Example: I waited all day for him to text me back. I’m such a clown.
Context: Commonly used in situations where someone feels embarrassed or tricked.
Informal_Text: I hung around all day, hoping he'd hit me up. What a goofball, right?
Informal_Text_Without_Slang: I waited all day for his message, feeling like an absolute fool.
Formal_Text: I spent the entire day waiting for his response, yet here I am, feeling rather foolish.

Example: That old tweet was so cringy, I can’t believe I posted that.
Context: Often used to describe social faux pas or embarrassing moments.
Informal_Text: Man, that old tweet was super awkward, can't believe I put that out there.
Informal_Text_Without_Slang: Man, that old tweet was embarrassingly lame – I can't believe I shared it.
Formal_Text: That antiquated tweet was exceedingly awkward and unrefined; it is astonishing that I published such content.

Example: I have major FOMO after seeing everyone’s vacation pics.
Context: Often used to describe the feeling of missing out on something exciting, especially in social media contexts.
Informal_Text: Man, I'm really kicking myself for missing out on all those vacation snaps!
Informal_Text_Without_Slang: I'm really kicking myself for missing out on those vacation pictures!
Formal_Text: I experience a considerable apprehension about missing out on enjoyable experiences, having observed the travel photographs shared by others.

Example: You’re moving to LA? Fr?
Context: Common in digital conversations to confirm or emphasize sincerity.
Informal_Text: Yo, you're really moving to LA?
Informal_Text_Without_Slang: Are you actually moving to LA?
Formal_Text: Indeed, you're relocating to Los Angeles? Truly?

Description: an expression commonly used when someone is feeling either so overjoyed or exasperated that they can’t even find the right words; depending on the context.
Example: Ion even care what they think.
Context: Often used in casual or informal conversations.
Informal_Text: I'm utterly indifferent to their opinions.
Informal_Text_Without_Slang: I don't care at all about their opinion.
Formal_Text: I could not care less about their opinions.

Example: This meme is too much, I can’t even!
Context: Popular in social media culture to express being speechless or amused.
Informal_Text: This meme's too much, ain't nobody got time for that!
Informal_Text_Without_Slang: This meme is too much for me to handle!
Formal_Text: This meme is excessively overwhelming; I am genuinely unable to cope.

Example: Let’s meet IRL next week.
Context: Commonly used in online spaces to differentiate between virtual and real-life interactions.
Informal_Text: Let's hook up offline next week.
Informal_Text_Without_Slang: Let's hook up in person next week.
Formal_Text: Shall we arrange a face-to-face meeting next week?

Description: A stereotype for women who behave extremely unreasonably and childish – especially towards service staff or people of colour – and tend to invoke their racial privilege
Example: That woman asked to speak to the manager, total Karen move.
Context: Widely used in social media to describe someone acting entitled or rude, typically in public situations.
Informal_Text: She really went and pulled a diva fit, totally Mabel behavior.
Informal_Text_Without_Slang: That lady demanded to talk to the supervisor, very entitled behavior.
Formal_Text: The woman demanded to address the supervisor, displaying highly inappropriate behavior.

Example: I’m low key excited about the new movie.
Context: Used to express a feeling or action that is kept relatively quiet or understated.
Informal_Text: I'm kinda hyped up 'bout that fresh flick.
Informal_Text_Without_Slang: I'm sort of secretly excited about the new movie.
Formal_Text: I'm rather quietly enthusiastic about the upcoming film.

Description: It just means to admire or look up to someone so much that you jokingly want to be adopted by them or have them as your second parent
Example: Beyoncé is such a mom.
Context: Often used in stan culture to refer to female celebrities or figures who inspire admiration.
Informal_Text: Beyoncé's just my idol!
Informal_Text_Without_Slang: Beyoncé is just so inspiring that I wish she were my role model!
Formal_Text: Beyoncé is truly someone to greatly admire.

Description: It just means to admire or look up to someone so much that you jokingly want to be adopted by them or have them as your second parent
Example: Keanu Reeves is my dad.
Context: Used in a playful manner to express admiration for men who are respected or seen as role models.
Informal_Text: Man, I'd swap my old man for Keanu Reeves any day!
Informal_Text_Without_Slang: I absolutely adore Keanu Reeves and would be thrilled to have him as a second father figure.
Formal_Text: I deeply admire and hold Keanu Reeves in such high regard that it's as if I wish to be under his care, much like a son would desire to have him as a second father figure.

Example: NGL, that was a tough workout.
Context: Frequently used in conversations to preface honesty or a blunt opinion.
Informal_Text: Ain't Gonna Sugarcoat It, That Was a Tough Workout.
Informal_Text_Without_Slang: To be honest, that was quite a challenging workout.
Formal_Text: Frankly speaking, that was indeed a challenging workout.

Description: Pick me girls are the type of girls who claim that they are nothing like other girls, in order to get attention from guys (also see ‘simping’ below). It’s a derogatory term.
Example: She’s such a pick me girl, always saying she’s not like other girls.
Context: Often used in a critical way to call out behavior aimed at seeking validation.
Informal_Text: She's pure drama queen, constantly boasting she's different from the rest of 'em.
Informal_Text_Without_Slang: She's such a self-proclaimed exceptional woman, constantly emphasizing her differences from ordinary females.
Formal_Text: She is quite self-proclaimed distinctive, frequently asserting her distinctiveness from other women.

Description: Short for ‘baby boomer’, referring to older folks born 1946 to 1964 – but mostly used to clap back at pretty much anyone who’s older and not so in-the-know.
Example: My boss is such a boomer, doesn’t even know how to use Zoom.
Context: Often used humorously or critically to highlight generational differences.
Informal_Text: Old man can't figure out Zoom, my boss is clueless!
Informal_Text_Without_Slang: My boss is really out of touch, can't figure out how to use Zoom.
Formal_Text: The manager exhibits a certain lack of familiarity with contemporary technology, as evidenced by his inability to utilize Zoom effectively.

Description: When you "sleep on" something, you overlook or underestimate it
Example: You’re sleeping on this new album, it’s so good.
Context: Often used to draw attention to something underrated.
Informal_Text: You're really missing out on that new album, it's fantastic!
Informal_Text_Without_Slang: You're really overlooking that new album; it's fantastic.
Formal_Text: Overlooking the merit of that latest album seems unwarranted; it's exceptionally good.

Description: Diss. Also: throwing shade; being shady.
Example: She was throwing shade at my outfit.
Context: Commonly used in discussions of gossip or social conflict, particularly when the insult is indirect.
Informal_Text: She was obviously dissing my getup.
Informal_Text_Without_Slang: She was subtly criticizing my clothing choice.
Formal_Text: She was criticizing my choice of attire subtly.

Example: I was shook when I found out the news.
Context: Often used to describe being emotionally or mentally impacted by something unexpected.
Informal_Text: Man, that news left me stunned!
Informal_Text_Without_Slang: Flabbergasted is how I felt when I learned about the news.
Formal_Text: I was utterly astonished upon learning the news.

Description: Shake my head’. Another one for texting, smh usually signifies exasperation
Example: You forgot your homework again? Smh.
Context: Common in texting or social media to signal mild frustration or disappointment.
Informal_Text: Man, you left your homework again? Sigh.
Informal_Text_Without_Slang: Goodness, you left your homework again?
Formal_Text: Once more, you've overlooked your homework? Tsk tsk.

Description: short for “to be honest” and is usually used when making a comment or a joke (best to stick to texts with this one too).
Example: TBH, I didn’t enjoy the party last night.
Context: Often used to preface a blunt opinion or honest confession.
Informal_Text: To be honest, I wasn't feeling the vibe at that party last night.
Informal_Text_Without_Slang: To be honest, I didn't have a good time at the party last night.
Formal_Text: To be frank, I did not find the party enjoyable last night.

Description: Stands for desperate, usually for attention
Example: He’s been texting me nonstop, he’s so thirsty.
Context: Often used to describe behavior that appears desperate for attention or validation.
Informal_Text: He can't stop messaging me, he's really desperate.
Informal_Text_Without_Slang: He's constantly messaging me, he's quite desperate for attention.
Formal_Text: He has been persistently messaging me, indicating an excessive desire for attention.

Description: a social media post intended to, uh, entice viewers and get attention.
Example: She posted a total thirst trap on Instagram.
Context: Common in social media, where people post images to garner likes or comments based on physical appearance.
Informal_Text: She straight-up posted an attention-grabbing pic on Insta.
Informal_Text_Without_Slang: She shared an irresistible attention-grabber on Instagram.
Formal_Text: She intentionally posted an alluring image on Instagram to attract attention.

Description: A very enthusiastic and celebratory way of saying yes!
Example: Yas queen! You’re slaying that outfit!
Context: Popular in LGBTQ+ and online cultures to express excitement, approval, or support.
Informal_Text: Absolutely slaying it, girlfriend!
Informal_Text_Without_Slang: Absolutely, girl! You're rocking that look!
Formal_Text: Indeed, you are absolutely radiant in that ensemble!

Description: The Gen Z version of YOLO (you only live once). Usually exclaimed (pretty loudly) when doing something risky or throwing an item very hard (most of the time for absolutely no reason at all and with absolutely no aim).
Example: He yeeted the ball across the yard.
Context: Often used in a playful, exaggerated manner, especially in meme culture.
Informal_Text: He chuck'd that ball way across the yard!
Informal_Text_Without_Slang: He flung the ball recklessly across the yard!
Formal_Text: He carelessly hurled the ball across the yard with reckless abandon.

Description: used to express disgust at something unpleasant or offensive.
Example: He talks with his mouth full, that gave me the ick.
Context: Frequently used in dating scenarios to describe a moment that turns someone off.
Informal_Text: Man, talking with a mouthful is just gross - totally gives me the eww!
Informal_Text_Without_Slang: Talking with a mouthful leaves me feeling rather disgusted.
Formal_Text: His eating manners are rather unsightly; they evoke a sense of distaste in me.

Description: means no or know. It functions as a more dramatic way of saying "no" or "know," and sounds like "no" with an Australian accent.
Example: Naur, why did you do that?
Context: Often used humorously in memes or texts, exaggerating the word for comedic effect.
Informal_Text: Mate, what's the story with that?
Informal_Text_Without_Slang: Why on earth did you do that?
Formal_Text: Indeed, why have you taken such an action?

Description: A shortened version of "say no more."
Example: Want to grab dinner? Say less, I’m there.
Context: Used to quickly agree with a suggestion or plan.
Informal_Text: Wanna catch a bite? That's all I need to hear, I'm in.
Informal_Text_Without_Slang: Ready for dinner? Count me in.
Formal_Text: Shall we have dinner together? Needless to say, I will be present.

Description: a more fun way of saying something or someone is ridiculous, or that it can't be taken seriously.
Example: You’re being so unserious about this important issue.
Context: Used to point out lack of gravity or responsibility in someone’s actions.
Informal_Text: You're really goofing off about this crucial matter!
Informal_Text_Without_Slang: You're really not taking this seriously enough, it's quite a significant matter.
Formal_Text: Your approach to this critical matter appears remarkably frivolous.

Description: To be “gagged” is to be shocked, amazed, et cetera.
Example: I was gagged when I saw her outfit!
Context: Frequently used in drag and LGBTQ+ culture to express astonishment or awe.
Informal_Text: Man, I was floored by her getup!
Informal_Text_Without_Slang: I was utterly astonished by her attire!
Formal_Text: I was utterly astonished by her attire!

Description: If you “ate” something, it means you executed it extremely well.
Example: She ate that performance, no crumbs left.
Context: Popular in stan culture, especially in discussions about performances, fashion, or style.
Informal_Text: She nailed that performance, not a single trace left behind.
Informal_Text_Without_Slang: Nailed it! Not a trace left behind.
Formal_Text: She delivered that performance flawlessly, leaving nothing to be desired.

Example: You won the game? Poggers!
Context: Popular in gaming and streaming culture to celebrate exciting moments.
Informal_Text: Dang, you won the game? That's sick!
Informal_Text_Without_Slang: Wow, you won the game! Fantastic!
Formal_Text: You've triumphantly won the game! Bravo!

Description: any lovely person who seems like they’re the main character, evoking as much admiration as jealousy
Example: She’s such a Heather, everyone loves her.
Context: Used to describe someone who is effortlessly perfect and adored by others.
Informal_Text: Man, she's sure got that charisma that makes everyone adore her, yet leaves some green with envy too!
Informal_Text_Without_Slang: She's absolutely captivating, everyone adores her.
Formal_Text: She is truly captivating, garnering admiration from all who know her.

Example: You like pizza? I’m with it.
Context: Often used to quickly express agreement or solidarity in casual conversation.
Informal_Text: Are you into pizza? I'm totally on board with that!
Informal_Text_Without_Slang: Are you fond of pizza? I'm totally on board with that.
Formal_Text: You appreciate pizza? I am entirely in agreement.

Description: Used to describe someone showing off, gloating, or parading around.
Example: He’s flexing his new car all over social media.
Context: Common in contexts where someone is showing off something impressive, often in a boastful way.
Informal_Text: He's flaunting that fresh whip everywhere on socials.
Informal_Text_Without_Slang: He's flaunting his new car everywhere on social media.
Formal_Text: He is ostentatiously displaying his newly acquired automobile across various social media platforms.

Description: term born out of the popularity of the high-end fashion brand. These days, it means that something is good
Example: Everything is Gucci, don’t worry.
Context: Used casually to express that things are going well or to describe something stylish.
Informal_Text: All good, don't stress it.
Informal_Text_Without_Slang: Everything's all good, don't fret.
Formal_Text: Everything is in order, there is no need for concern.

Description: Hands down one of the biggest slang terms to hit pop culture in the summer of 2019, hot girl summer is about women having a good time and being unapologetic about who they are
Example: I’m ready for hot girl summer this year!
Context: Popularized by Megan Thee Stallion, it’s used to promote independence and fun.
Informal_Text: I'm all set for a rad summer this year!
Informal_Text_Without_Slang: I'm all set for a fabulous, carefree summer this year!
Formal_Text: I am prepared for a season of self-expression and enjoyment as a woman this year.

Description: used to describe someone's dance moves. It's usually used in the phrase "get sturdy", which means that someone is performing a specific type of dance in which they move their legs, spin, and hop.
Example: He’s so sturdy on the dance floor!
Context: Commonly used in urban slang to describe confidence and strength, especially in physical performance.
Informal_Text: He's really killing it on the dance floor!
Informal_Text_Without_Slang: He really knows how to throw down some moves on the dance floor!
Formal_Text: He exhibits an impressive agility on the dance floor.

Description: used to blame someone for their own loss.
Example: You can’t beat the level? Sounds like a skill issue.
Context: Frequently used in gaming communities to tease someone for struggling.
Informal_Text: Can't crack that level, huh? Must be some serious skill problems on your end.
Informal_Text_Without_Slang: Struggling with that level, huh? Seems more like a talent problem to me.
Formal_Text: It appears that you're struggling to clear the level. This could suggest a matter of skill.

Example: That meme is TNTL-worthy!
Context: Often used in humorous contexts to signal a challenge not to laugh, commonly seen in social media videos.
Informal_Text: Man, that meme's hilarious as heck!
Informal_Text_Without_Slang: That meme's nearly uncontrollable!
Formal_Text: That meme is remarkably amusing!

Example: Sorry, G2G! Talk later!
Context: Frequently used in text messaging or online chats to quickly exit a conversation.
Informal_Text: Gotta scoot! Chat soon!
Informal_Text_Without_Slang: Alrighty then, gotta scram. Chat soon!
Formal_Text: I'm sorry, but I must leave now. Let's talk another time.

Example: I might move abroad one day, YNK.
Context: Commonly used in conversations about future possibilities or unknown outcomes.
Informal_Text: Ain't know where I'll end up tomorrow, could be overseas!
Informal_Text_Without_Slang: You never really know when I might move abroad.
Formal_Text: One can never be entirely certain, I might move abroad someday.

Example: That joke was hilarious, CSL!
Context: Common in texting or online conversations to emphasize uncontrollable laughter.
Informal_Text: Man, that joke cracked me up good!
Informal_Text_Without_Slang: That joke had me cracking up!
Formal_Text: That joke was absolutely hilarious, it left me in stitches!

Example: You bought the same shoes as me? GMTA!
Context: Typically used in friendly conversations to acknowledge a shared thought or action.
Informal_Text: Dang, you got the same kicks as me? Nailed it!
Informal_Text_Without_Slang: Bought the same shoes as you? Perfect sync!
Formal_Text: Remarkable coincidence indeed, you have purchased the identical footwear. Fascinating agreement!

Example: IMO, that movie wasn’t that great.
Context: Used to soften a statement, making it clear that it’s subjective.
Informal_Text: That film was meh, tbh.
Informal_Text_Without_Slang: In my opinion, that movie wasn't fantastic.
Formal_Text: In my opinion, that film was not particularly impressive.

Example: IMOH, this is the best pizza place in town.
Context: Commonly used in online discussions to share a polite or humble opinion.
Informal_Text: Gotta give ya my two cents here: This pizza joint's tops in town, no question!
Informal_Text_Without_Slang: In my humble opinion, this is the top-notch pizza spot in town.
Formal_Text: In my considered opinion, this is the superior pizza establishment within our town.

Example: You’re fired! JK, I could never fire you.
Context: Frequently used in casual conversations or texts to clarify humor.
Informal_Text: You're canned! Pfft, not a chance I'd ever let you go like that.
Informal_Text_Without_Slang: You're fired... just kidding, there's no way I could actually fire you.
Formal_Text: You are dismissed! However, in jest, I cannot dismiss you.

Description: Short for “baby." Often a pet name for a crush or significant other.
Example: I’m spending the weekend with my bae.
Context: Often used to refer to a romantic partner or someone you deeply care about.
Informal_Text: I'm hangin' with my baby this weekend.
Informal_Text_Without_Slang: Spending the weekend with my dear one.
Formal_Text: I am spending the weekend with my dear one.

Example: How’s it going? SSDD.
Context: Commonly used in conversations to express boredom or lack of excitement.
Informal_Text: What's up? More of the same, I see.
Informal_Text_Without_Slang: What's up? More of the same today.
Formal_Text: How is everything today? Business as usual.

Example: The beach is amazing, WYWH!
Context: Often sent from vacation spots or during fun events.
Informal_Text: Man, I'm loving this beach, sure wish you were here too!
Informal_Text_Without_Slang: What a stunning beach, I wish you were here!
Formal_Text: The beach is truly remarkable; I wish you could be here to experience it.

Description: Just like in sports, benching someone in dating means putting them to the side to date other people.
Example: I think he’s benching me—he texts but never makes plans.
Context: Often used in modern dating to describe a lack of serious intent.
Informal_Text: He's keeping you on standby - chats up a storm but ain't setting no dates.
Informal_Text_Without_Slang: He seems to be keeping me on standby - he messages regularly but never proposes any dates.
Formal_Text: It seems to me that he might be keeping me in reserve—he continually communicates, yet consistently avoids arranging meetings.

Description: When someone leads you on by flirting and making you feel special but without any intention to actually commit to a relationship.
Example: She’s breadcrumbing him, always texting but never wanting to meet.
Context: Describes inconsistent romantic or flirtatious communication.
Informal_Text: She's stringin' him along, constantly messaging yet avoiding face-to-face meetings.
Informal_Text_Without_Slang: She continually texts him, yet consistently avoids meeting up.
Formal_Text: She consistently communicates with him without any intention of arranging a face-to-face encounter.

Description: "Cuffing" simply means to get into a relationship.
Example: Everyone’s cuffing this fall, it’s relationship season.
Context: Often refers to the “cuffing season” when people seek partners to get through the winter.
Informal_Text: Everybody's hooking up this fall, it's all about coupling up!
Informal_Text_Without_Slang: Everyone's getting into relationships this fall, it's the time for coupling up.
Formal_Text: Everyone appears to be forming relationships this autumn; it seems to be the season for relationships.

Example: We need to DTR soon, I need to know where we stand.
Context: Used in dating to clarify whether a relationship is serious or casual.
Informal_Text: Let's chat about us, where things are headed. I gotta know what's up between us.
Informal_Text_Without_Slang: Let's clarify our situation soon; I need to understand where things are headed between us.
Formal_Text: It's essential that we clarify our current relationship status shortly, as I would like to understand our present situation more clearly.

Description: refers to a form of psychological manipulation in which a significant other makes you feel crazy or wrong, even when unjustified
Example: He keeps telling me I’m overreacting, but I think he’s gaslighting me.
Context: Often used to describe psychological manipulation in relationships or discussions.
Informal_Text: He's constantly making me feel like I'm losing my mind, but I reckon he's pulling a fast one on me.
Informal_Text_Without_Slang: He consistently makes me feel like I'm exaggerating, and I believe he might be deceiving me psychologically.
Formal_Text: He persistently suggests that I am excessively emotional, yet I suspect that he is engaging in a form of psychological manipulation, making me question my own perceptions or feelings.

Example: Goodnight, ILY!
Context: Frequently used in texting to express affection quickly.
Informal_Text: Nighty night, my love!
Informal_Text_Without_Slang: Goodnight, my dear, I truly care for you.
Formal_Text: Goodnight, my dear, I love you.

Description: Based on the idea of red flags, pink flags are on step down. They aren’t huge warning signals that something is wrong, but they can hint that this relationship isn’t super healthy
Example: She’s always late—kind of a pink flag, but not a dealbreaker.
